translations.literal: Now great power is not recovered, the heir apparent is not established, adopted sons are not reformed, discipline daily slips, customs daily decay, petty men daily advance, gentlemen daily retreat, scholarly morale daily falters, the avenue of remonstrance daily closes, honors daily grow cheap, bribery daily spreads, rites and music daily fall into disuse, punishments daily grow excessive, the people's wealth daily is exhausted, and military affairs daily decline.
translations.idiomatic: Now great power is not recovered, the heir apparent is not established, adopted sons are not reformed, discipline daily slips, customs daily decay, petty men daily advance, gentlemen daily retreat, scholarly morale daily falters, the avenue of remonstrance daily closes, honors daily grow cheap, bribery daily spreads, rites and music daily fall into disuse, punishments daily grow excessive, the people's wealth is daily exhausted, and military affairs daily decline.

sentences.zh: 瑾既誅矣，而善治一無可舉者，由陛下惑異端故也。

translations.literal: Jin was already executed, yet no good governance can be cited—this is because Your Majesty is deluded by heterodox teachings.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was already executed, yet no good governance can be cited—this is because Your Majesty is deluded by heterodox teachings.

sentences.zh: 夫禁掖嚴邃，豈異教所得雜居？

translations.literal: The forbidden inner palace is stern and deep—how can heterodox teachings be allowed to dwell there mixed in?
translations.idiomatic: The forbidden inner palace is stern and secluded—how can followers of heterodox teachings be allowed to live there?

sentences.zh: 今乃建寺西華門內，延止番僧，日與聚處。

translations.literal: Now a temple is built inside Xihua Gate, Tibetan monks are retained and lodged, and day by day they gather and dwell together.
translations.idiomatic: Now a temple has been built inside Xihua Gate, Tibetan monks have been invited to stay, and they gather there day after day.

sentences.zh: 異言日沃，忠言日遠，用舍顛倒，舉錯乖方。

translations.literal: Strange words daily pour in, loyal words daily recede, employment and dismissal are reversed, and actions and errors miss their mark.
translations.idiomatic: Heterodox counsel pours in daily while loyal remonstrance grows distant; appointments and dismissals are reversed, and every measure misses its mark.

sentences.zh: 政務廢馳，職此之故。

translations.literal: State affairs fall into neglect—this is the reason.
translations.idiomatic: State affairs have fallen into neglect for this very reason.

sentences.zh: 伏望陛下翻然悔悟，毀佛寺，出番僧，妙選儒臣，朝夕勸講，攬大權以絕天下之奸，建儲位以立天下之本，革義子以正天下之名，則所謂振紀綱、勵風俗、進君子、退小人諸事，可次第舉矣。

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will suddenly repent and awaken, destroy Buddhist temples, expel Tibetan monks, choose excellent Confucian officials for daily lecture morning and evening, gather great power to cut off all wickedness under Heaven, establish the heir to fix the foundation under Heaven, reform adopted sons to set right names under Heaven—then the matters called restoring discipline, encouraging custom, advancing gentlemen and retiring petty men can be carried out in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope Your Majesty will repent and awaken, destroy the Buddhist temples, expel the Tibetan monks, choose outstanding Confucian officials for daily instruction, consolidate supreme power to suppress wickedness throughout the realm, establish an heir to secure the foundation of the state, and abolish the practice of adopted sons to restore proper titles—then the tasks of restoring discipline, improving customs, advancing gentlemen, and dismissing petty men can be undertaken one after another.

sentences.zh: 」帝怒。

translations.literal: " The emperor was enraged.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was enraged.

sentences.zh: 罪將不測，以大臣救得免。

translations.literal: Punishment was immeasurable; he was spared because great ministers interceded.
translations.idiomatic: He faced immeasurable punishment but was spared through the intercession of senior ministers.

sentences.zh: 逾日，中旨謫廣東通衢驛丞。

translations.literal: The next day an imperial directive demoted him to postal station assistant at Tongqu in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: The next day an edict from the palace demoted him to postal station assistant at Tongqu in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 王守仁撫贛州，檄中參其軍事。

translations.literal: Wang Shouren governed Ganzhou and in his proclamation had Zhong join in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shouren governed Ganzhou, he had Zhong join his staff for military affairs by written order.

sentences.zh: 預平宸濠。

translations.literal: He took part in suppressing Chen Hao.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in suppressing Chen Hao's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 世宗踐阼，復故官。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor ascended the throne, Zhong was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shizong Emperor ascended the throne, Zhong was restored to his former office.

sentences.zh: 未任，擢廣東僉事。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post he was promoted to Guangdong vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, he was promoted to vice commissioner in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 再遷廣西提學副使，以身為教。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to Guangxi vice education commissioner and took his own conduct as instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to vice education commissioner in Guangxi, teaching by his own example.

sentences.zh: 擇諸生高等聚五經書院，五日一登堂講難。

translations.literal: He selected the highest-ranking students and gathered them at the Five Classics Academy, ascending the hall once every five days to lecture and debate.
translations.idiomatic: He selected the best students and gathered them at the Five Classics Academy, lecturing and debating in the hall once every five days.

sentences.zh: 三遷廣東右布政使。

translations.literal: On a third transfer he became Right Administration Commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: On his third transfer he became Right Administration Commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 忤總督及巡撫御史，坐以不稱職，當罷。

translations.literal: He offended the governor-general and the investigating censor and was judged unfit for office, due for dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: He offended the governor-general and the investigating censor and was judged unfit for office, facing dismissal.

sentences.zh: 霍韜署吏部事，稱中素廉節有才望，當留。

translations.literal: Huo Tao was acting head of the Ministry of Personnel and said Zhong had always been incorrupt with integrity and talent, and ought to be kept.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Tao, acting head of the Ministry of Personnel, said Zhong had always been incorrupt and talented and ought to be retained.

sentences.zh: 會政府有不悅者，降四川右參政。

translations.literal: As there were displeased persons in the government, he was demoted to Right Vice Commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: As some in the government were displeased with him, he was demoted to Right Vice Commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 十八年擢右僉都御史，巡撫山東。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and appointed to govern Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and appointed regional governor of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 歲歉，令民捕蝗者倍予谷，蝗絕而饑者濟。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he ordered that those who caught locusts be given double grain; the locusts were exterminated and the hungry were relieved.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year he ordered double grain payments for locust catchers; the locust plague ended and the hungry were fed.

sentences.zh: 擒劇盜關繼光，鄰境攘其功，中不與辯。

translations.literal: He captured the great bandit Guan Jiguang; neighboring jurisdictions usurped the credit, and Zhong did not argue.
translations.idiomatic: He captured the notorious bandit Guan Jiguang; neighboring jurisdictions claimed the credit, but Zhong did not dispute it.

sentences.zh: 進副都御史，總督南京糧儲。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief and made overall superintendent of Nanjing grain storage.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief and put in charge of Nanjing grain reserves.

sentences.zh: 御史金燦按四川時，嘗薦中。

translations.literal: When Censor Jin Can toured Sichuan he once recommended Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor Jin Can inspected Sichuan he had once recommended Zhong.

sentences.zh: 中不謝，燦憾之，至是摭他事誣劾。

translations.literal: Zhong did not thank him; Can resented this, and at this time gathered other matters to falsely impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong never thanked him; Can resented this and now dredged up other matters to impeach him on false charges.

sentences.zh: 方議調用而中卒。

translations.literal: Just as transfer was under discussion Zhong died.
translations.idiomatic: Just as a transfer was being discussed, Zhong died.

sentences.zh: 光宗時，追謚莊介。

translations.literal: In the time of the Guangzong Emperor posthumous title Zhuangjie was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangzong reign he was posthumously granted the title Zhuangjie.

sentences.zh: 中守官廉。

translations.literal: Zhong in holding office was incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong served as an incorrupt official.

sentences.zh: 自廣西歸，欲飯客，貸米鄰家。

translations.literal: Returning from Guangxi he wished to feast guests and borrowed rice from a neighbor.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from Guangxi he wanted to entertain guests and borrowed rice from a neighbor.

sentences.zh: 米至，又乏薪，將以浴器爨。

translations.literal: When the rice arrived he again lacked firewood and was about to cook with a bath vessel.
translations.idiomatic: When the rice arrived he still had no firewood and was about to cook with a bathing tub.

sentences.zh: 會日已暮，竟不及飯而別。

translations.literal: As the day had already grown dark, in the end he parted without being able to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Evening came before he could eat, and his guests departed unfed.

sentences.zh: 少學於同里楊珠，既而擴充之，沈潛邃密，學者稱谷平先生。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Yang Zhu of the same district, later expanded upon it, plunged deep and was profound; scholars called him Master Guping.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied under Yang Zhu of his home district, then developed that learning further; steeped in profound scholarship, he was known to scholars as Master Guping.

sentences.zh: 門人羅洪先、王龜年、周子恭皆能傳其學。

translations.literal: Disciples Luo Hongxian, Wang Guinian, and Zhou Zigong all could transmit his learning.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples Luo Hongxian, Wang Guinian, and Zhou Zigong all carried on his teaching.

sentences.zh: 中族人楷，又傳洪先之學。

translations.literal: Zhong's clansman Kai again transmitted Hongxian's learning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong's clansman Kai in turn carried on Hongxian's teaching.

sentences.zh: 楷，字邦正。

translations.literal: Kai, courtesy name Bangzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Kai, styled Bangzheng.

sentences.zh: 由舉人授湯溪知縣。

translations.literal: Through the provincial graduate degree he was appointed magistrate of Tangxi.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate, he was appointed magistrate of Tangxi.

sentences.zh: 母艱服闋，補青田。

translations.literal: After mourning for his mother ended he was reassigned to Qingtian.
translations.idiomatic: After completing mourning for his mother, he was reassigned to Qingtian.

sentences.zh: 時倭躪東南，楷積谷資守禦。

translations.literal: At the time Japanese pirates ravaged the southeast; Kai stockpiled grain to support defense.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Japanese pirates ravaged the southeast; Kai stockpiled grain to support the defenses.

sentences.zh: 青田故無城。

translations.literal: Qingtian originally had no wall.
translations.idiomatic: Qingtian had no city wall.

sentences.zh: 倭至，楷禦於沙埠，倭不得渡，乃以間築城。

translations.literal: When the Japanese came Kai defended at Shabu; the Japanese could not cross, and he thereby found an interval to build a wall.
translations.idiomatic: When the pirates arrived Kai held them at Shabu; unable to cross, they withdrew, and he used the interval to build city walls.

sentences.zh: 倭又至，登陴守，日殺賊數人，倭遁去。

translations.literal: The Japanese came again; he mounted the ramparts to defend, killing several bandits each day, and the Japanese fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the pirates returned he manned the ramparts, killing several each day until they fled.

sentences.zh: 改知昌樂，亦以治行聞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to magistrate of Changle and was also known for administrative conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to magistrate of Changle, where he was also known for effective governance.

sentences.zh: 歐陽鐸，字崇道，泰和人。

translations.literal: Ouyang Duo, courtesy name Chongdao, was a native of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Duo, styled Chongdao, was from Taihe.

sentences.zh: 正德三年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the third year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 授行人。

translations.literal: He was appointed courier.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a courier in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 上書極論時政，不報。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial thoroughly discussing current policy; no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial vigorously criticizing current policy, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 使蜀府，王厚遺之，不受。

translations.literal: On mission to the Shu princely establishment, Wang generously gifted him; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: While on mission to the princely establishment of Shu, Wang tried to lavish gifts on him, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 歷工部郎中，改南兵部。

translations.literal: He served as a director in the Ministry of Works and was transferred to the Ministry of War at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a director in the Ministry of Works and was transferred to the Nanjing Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 出為延平知府。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Yanping.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Yanping.

sentences.zh: 毀淫祠數十百所，以其材葺學宮。

translations.literal: He destroyed several tens of illicit shrines and used their timber to repair the school hall.
translations.idiomatic: He destroyed dozens of illicit shrines and used their timber to repair the school precinct.

sentences.zh: 司禮太監蕭敬家奴殺人，置之法。

translations.literal: A household slave of the Directorate of Ceremonial eunuch Xiao Jing killed a man; Duo had him executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: When a household slave of the eunuch Xiao Jing of the Directorate of Ceremonial murdered someone, Duo had him punished by law.

sentences.zh: 調福州，議均徭曰：「郡多士大夫，其士大夫又多田產。

translations.literal: Transferred to Fuzhou, discussing equal corvée he said: "The prefecture has many literati, and those literati also have much land.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Fuzhou, he proposed equalizing corvée obligations: "This prefecture has many gentlemen, and they also hold most of the land.

sentences.zh: 民有產者無幾耳，而徭則盡責之民。

translations.literal: Commoners with property are few indeed, yet corvée is entirely charged to commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Few commoners own property, yet corvée labor falls entirely on them.

sentences.zh: 請分民半役。

translations.literal: I request that commoners bear half the service.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that gentlemen and commoners each bear half the labor obligations.

sentences.zh: 」士大夫率不便。

translations.literal: " The literati generally found it inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: " The gentry generally objected.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史汪珊力持之，議乃行。

translations.literal: Investigating censor Wang Shan struck forcefully in support, and the proposal was then carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Wang Shan forcefully upheld the proposal, and it was adopted.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年擢廣東提學副使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing he was promoted to Guangdong vice education commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiajing he was promoted to vice education commissioner in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 累遷南京光祿卿，歷右副都御史，巡撫應天十府。

translations.literal: He rose by stages to Director of Imperial Entertainment at Nanjing, served as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, and governed the ten prefectures of Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director of Imperial Entertainment at Nanjing, then served as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and regional governor of the ten Yingtian prefectures.

sentences.zh: 蘇、松田不甚相懸。

translations.literal: Land in Su and Song was not greatly unequal.
translations.idiomatic: Landholdings in Suzhou and Songjiang were not greatly unequal in size.

sentences.zh: 下者畝五升，上者至二十倍。

translations.literal: The lower paid five sheng per mu, the upper up to twenty times that.
translations.idiomatic: Lower-grade fields paid five sheng per mu in tax, while the highest paid as much as twenty times that.

sentences.zh: 鐸令賦最重者減耗米，派輕賫；

translations.literal: Duo ordered those with the heaviest assessments to reduce surcharge grain and assign lighter surcharges;
translations.idiomatic: Duo ordered those with the heaviest tax assessments to reduce surcharge grain and shift lighter surcharges to them;

sentences.zh: 最輕者征本色，增耗米。

translations.literal: the lightest to collect in kind and increase surcharge grain.
translations.idiomatic: while those with the lightest assessments paid in kind and took on increased surcharge grain.

sentences.zh: 陰輕重之，賦乃均。

translations.literal: Secretly lightening and heavifying, the tax became even.
translations.idiomatic: By quietly redistributing the burden, taxes were equalized.

sentences.zh: 諸推收田，從圩不從戶，詭寄無所容。

translations.literal: For all reassigned collection land, follow dyke enclosures not households; fraudulent registration had nowhere to hide.
translations.idiomatic: For all reassigned tax land, registration followed dyke enclosures rather than households, leaving no room for fraudulent shifting of obligations.

sentences.zh: 州縣荒田四千四百余頃，歲勒民償賦。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties had more than four thousand four hundred qing of abandoned land; each year commoners were forced to make up the tax.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties had more than 4,400 qing of abandoned farmland, and each year the people were forced to pay tax on it.

sentences.zh: 鐸以所清漏賦及他奇羨補之。

translations.literal: Duo used recovered leaked tax and other surplus revenue to make up for it.
translations.idiomatic: Duo made up the shortfall from recovered uncollected taxes and other surplus revenue.

sentences.zh: 議徭役及裁郵置費凡數十百條，民皆稱便。

translations.literal: He proposed dozens of items on corvée and cutting postal expenses; the people all called it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted dozens of proposals on corvée labor and cutting postal expenses, all of which the people found beneficial.

sentences.zh: 遷南京兵部侍郎，進吏部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of War at Nanjing and advanced to Right Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of War at Nanjing and promoted to Right Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 九廟災，自陳去。

translations.literal: When the Nine Temples burned he petitioned to resign.
translations.idiomatic: After the fire at the Nine Temples he offered his resignation.

sentences.zh: 鐸有文學，內行修潔。

translations.literal: Duo had literary talent and inward conduct refined and pure.
translations.idiomatic: Duo was a man of letters with refined private conduct.

sentences.zh: 仕雖通顯，家具蕭然。

translations.literal: Though his office was eminent, his household furnishings were sparse.
translations.idiomatic: Though he rose to high office, his household remained austere.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈工部尚書，謚恭簡。

translations.literal: On death he was posthumously made Minister of Works and given the posthumous title Gongjian.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Minister of Works and granted the posthumous title Gongjian.

sentences.zh: 陶諧，字世和，會稽人。

translations.literal: Tao Xie, courtesy name Shihe, was a native of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Xie, styled Shihe, was from Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 弘治八年鄉試第一。

translations.literal: First in the provincial examination in the eighth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked first in the provincial examination in the eighth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 明年成進士，選庶吉士，授工科給事中。

translations.literal: The next year he became a jinshi, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed supervising secretary of the Ministry of Works section.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works section.

sentences.zh: 請命儒臣日講《大學衍義》，孝宗嘉納之。

translations.literal: He requested that Confucian officials daily lecture on the Daxue Yanyi; the Xiaozong Emperor commended and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Confucian officials lecture daily on the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning, and the Xiaozong Emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 正德改元，劉瑾等亂政。

translations.literal: At the change of reign title in Zhengde, Liu Jin and others disrupted government.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhengde reign began, Liu Jin and his faction threw the government into disorder.

sentences.zh: 諧請以瑾等誤國罪告先帝，罪之勿赦。

translations.literal: Xie requested that Jin and others be charged before the late emperor with the crime of ruining the state, punished without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Xie requested that Jin and his associates be charged before the late emperor with the crime of ruining the state and punished without pardon.

sentences.zh: 瑾摘其譌字令對狀，伏罪乃宥之。

translations.literal: Jin picked out his erroneous characters and ordered him to answer charges; only after admitting guilt was he pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Jin seized on a textual error and forced him to face judgment; only after admitting guilt was he spared.

sentences.zh: 帝命中官崔杲等往江南、浙江織造，杲等復乞長蘆鹽引。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered eunuchs Cui Gao and others to go to Jiangnan and Zhejiang for weaving; Gao and others again begged for Changlu salt certificates.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent eunuchs such as Cui Gao to Jiangnan and Zhejiang to supervise weaving, and Gao again requested Changlu salt certificates.

sentences.zh: 諧再疏爭，皆不聽。

translations.literal: Xie twice submitted memorials to dispute it; all went unheeded.
translations.idiomatic: Xie memorialized twice in protest, but both times his objections went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 諧當出理邊儲，以工科掌印無人，請俟行日遣官代署。

translations.literal: Xie was due to go out to manage frontier stores; as no one held the seal in the Works section he requested that on the day of departure an official be sent to act in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Xie was soon to leave to manage frontier grain stores; as no one else held the Works-section seal, he asked that an official be sent to act for him when he departed.

sentences.zh: 瑾遂中諧，下詔獄廷杖，斥為民。

translations.literal: Jin then struck at Xie; he was put in the imperial prison, beaten at court, and expelled as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Jin then set a trap for Xie, who was imprisoned, beaten at court, and stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 旋榜為奸黨。

translations.literal: Soon he was posted on the list of treacherous partisans.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon listed among the treacherous faction.

sentences.zh: 又誣以巡視十庫時缺布不奏，復械至闕下杖之，謫戍肅州。

translations.literal: Again he was falsely charged for failing to report cloth shortages when inspecting the ten treasuries; he was again shackled to the palace gate and beaten, and banished to garrison at Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then falsely accused of failing to report cloth shortages during an inspection of the ten treasuries, beaten again at the palace gates, and exiled to Suzhou as a soldier.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，釋還鄉，其黨猶用事，竟不獲召。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed he was released to return home; Jin's faction still held power, and in the end he was not recalled.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin was executed he was released and returned home, but Jin's allies still held power and he was never recalled.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年復官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing he was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiajing he was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 未至，除江西僉事，轉河南管河副使。

translations.literal: Before he arrived he was appointed Jiangxi vice commissioner and transferred to Henan vice commissioner for river management.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up his post he was appointed vice commissioner in Jiangxi, then transferred to vice commissioner for river management in Henan.

sentences.zh: 命沿河植柳，傍藝葭葦，有事采以為埽。

translations.literal: He was ordered to plant willows along the river and cultivate reeds beside them; when needed they were gathered for dikes.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered willows planted along the riverbanks and reeds cultivated beside them, to be harvested for river dikes when needed.

sentences.zh: 總理都御史請推行之諸道，歲省費鉅萬。

translations.literal: The supervising censor-in-chief requested extending this to all circuits; each year expenses were saved by tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising censor-in-chief asked that the policy be extended to all circuits, saving tens of thousands of taels each year.

sentences.zh: 遷參政，歷左、右布政使，皆在河南。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice commissioner and served as left and right administration commissioner, all in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice commissioner and served successively as Left and Right Administration Commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢右副都御史，提督南、贛、汀、漳軍務。

translations.literal: After a long time he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and put in charge of military affairs in Nan, Gan, Ting, and Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and put in charge of military affairs in southern Jiangxi and southern Fujian.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「守令遷太驟，宜以六年為期。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: "Magistrates and prefects are transferred too hastily; six years ought to be the term.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he wrote: "Magistrates and prefects are transferred too frequently; a six-year term would be appropriate.

sentences.zh: 言官忤旨，當優容。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials who offend the intent ought to be treated with favor.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials who offend the throne ought to be treated with forbearance.

sentences.zh: 養病官才力堪任者，毋終棄。

translations.literal: Sick-leave officials whose talent and strength can bear office must not be finally abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Officials on sick leave whose talents still qualify them for office should not be permanently cast aside.

sentences.zh: 」時南京御史馬敭等劾王瓊被逮，而新例養病久者率不復收敘，故諧以為言。

translations.literal: " At the time Nanjing censor Ma Yang and others impeached Wang Qiong and were arrested, and under the new rule those long on sick leave generally were not again employed—therefore Xie spoke on this.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time Nanjing Censor Ma Yang and others were arrested for impeaching Wang Qiong, and under a new rule officials on long sick leave were generally not reappointed—hence Xie's memorial.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「今天下差徭煩重。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Today corvée levies under Heaven are troublesome and heavy.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "Corvée levies throughout the realm have become burdensome.

sentences.zh: 既有河夫、機兵、打手、富戶、力士諸役，乃編審裏甲，復征曠丁課及供億諸費。

translations.literal: Already there are river laborers, militia soldiers, brawlers, wealthy households, and strongmen among the services; then lijia registration is compiled and reviewed, and vacant-household levies and supply expenses are again collected.
translations.idiomatic: In addition to river laborers, militia soldiers, brawlers, wealthy households, and strongmen, the lijia system was recompiled and fees for vacant households and supply costs were levied again.

sentences.zh: 乞皆罷免。

translations.literal: I beg that all be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that all of these be abolished.

sentences.zh: 」帝采納之。

translations.literal: " The emperor adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor adopted his proposals.

sentences.zh: 尋遷兵部右侍郎，總督兩廣軍務。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Right Vice Minister of War and made overall commander of military affairs in the Two Guangs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of War and put in overall command of military affairs in Guangdong and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 海寇陳邦瑞、許折桂等突入波羅廟，欲犯廣州，為指揮李筜所蹙。

translations.literal: Sea bandits Chen Bangrui, Xu Zhegui, and others suddenly entered Boluo Temple, intending to attack Guangzhou, but were pressed by Commander Li Dang.
translations.idiomatic: Sea bandits Chen Bangrui, Xu Zhegui, and others suddenly entered Boluo Temple intending to attack Guangzhou, but were driven back by Commander Li Dang.

sentences.zh: 邦瑞投水死，折桂還所執指揮二人，乞就撫。

translations.literal: Bangrui threw himself into the water and died; Zhegui returned the two commanders he had seized and begged to accept pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Bangrui drowned himself; Zhegui returned the two commanders he had captured and asked to submit to pacification.

sentences.zh: 諧居折桂等東莞，編為總甲，使約束其黨五百人為新民。

translations.literal: Xie settled Zhegui and the others in Dongguan, organized them as zongjia units, and had them restrain their five hundred followers as new subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Xie settled Zhegui and his followers in Dongguan, organized them into zongjia units, and had them keep their five hundred followers in line as new subjects.

sentences.zh: 兵部以降賊群聚，恐乘隙為變，令解散其黨。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War, fearing that surrendered bandits gathered together might seize an opportunity to rebel, ordered their followers dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War, fearing that the surrendered bandits might rebel if left gathered together, ordered their followers dispersed.

sentences.zh: 已，陽春賊趙林花等攻城，與德慶賊鳳二全相倚為患，諧討破百二十五砦。

translations.literal: Soon after, bandits Zhao Linhua and others of Yangchun attacked a city and, relying on Feng Erquan and other bandits of Deqing as mutual support, caused trouble; Xie attacked and broke one hundred twenty-five stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Yangchun bandits led by Zhao Linhua attacked a city and, backed by Deqing bandit Feng Erquan, caused trouble; Xie attacked and destroyed 125 stockades.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「諧功足錄，第前縱患者誰？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Xie's merit is enough to be recorded—but who earlier indulged the troublemakers?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Xie's merit deserves recognition—but who earlier indulged the troublemakers?

sentences.zh: 」乃僅賚銀幣。

translations.literal: " He then granted only silver and silks.
translations.idiomatic: " He then granted only silver and silks.

sentences.zh: 瓊山沙灣洞賊黎佛二等殺典史，諧復剿平。

translations.literal: Bandits Li Fo'er and others of Shawan Cave in Qiongshan killed a registrar; Xie again suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fo'er and other bandits of Shawan Cave in Qiongshan killed a registrar; Xie again suppressed and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 為總督三年，俘斬累萬。

translations.literal: As governor-general for three years he captured and killed tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: As governor-general for three years he captured and killed tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home upon mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 起兵部左侍郎。

translations.literal: He was raised to Left Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 九廟災，自陳致仕歸。

translations.literal: When the Nine Temples burned he petitioned to retire and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After the fire at the Nine Temples he petitioned to retire and returned home.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈兵部尚書。

translations.literal: On death he was posthumously made Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，謚莊敏。

translations.literal: Early in Longqing the posthumous title Zhuangmin was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Longqing reign he was posthumously granted the title Zhuangmin.

sentences.zh: 孫大順，字景熙。

translations.literal: Sun Dashun, courtesy name Jingxi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Dashun, styled Jingxi.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十五年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the forty-fifth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the forty-fifth year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 歷官福建右布政使。

translations.literal: He served in office up to Right Administration Commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Right Administration Commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 司帑失銀，吏卒五十人皆坐系。

translations.literal: When the treasury lost silver, fifty clerks and runners were all imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When silver was lost from the treasury, fifty clerks and runners were all imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 大順言於左使曰：「盜者兩三人耳，何盡系之為？

translations.literal: Dashun said to the left commissioner: "The thieves are only two or three people—why imprison them all?
translations.idiomatic: Dashun said to the left commissioner: "There are only two or three thieves—why imprison everyone?

sentences.zh: 請為公治之。

translations.literal: I request to handle this for you.
translations.idiomatic: Allow me to handle this for you.

sentences.zh: 」乃縱囚令跡盜，果得真者。

translations.literal: " He then released the prisoners and had them track the thieves, and indeed found the real culprits.
translations.idiomatic: " He then released the prisoners and had them track down the thieves, and the real culprits were found.

sentences.zh: 終右副都御史，廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: He ended as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and governor of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and regional governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 弟大臨，字虞臣。

translations.literal: Younger brother Dalin, courtesy name Yuchen.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Dalin, styled Yuchen.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十五年進士及第，授編修。

translations.literal: Metropolitan graduate in the thirty-fifth year of Jiajing and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He placed among the top graduates in the thirty-fifth year of Jiajing and was appointed a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 吳時來劾嚴嵩，大臨為定疏草。

translations.literal: When Wu Shilai impeached Yan Song, Dalin drafted the memorial for him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Shilai impeached Yan Song, Dalin drafted the memorial for him.

sentences.zh: 時來下詔獄，詰所共謀。

translations.literal: When Shilai was put in the imperial prison he was questioned about his co-conspirators.
translations.idiomatic: When Shilai was imprisoned he was questioned about his co-conspirators.

sentences.zh: 大臨不顧，日餉之藥物，時來亦忍死無一言。

translations.literal: Dalin paid no heed and daily supplied him with medicine and food; Shilai also endured death without a single word.
translations.idiomatic: Dalin ignored the inquiry and daily supplied him with medicine and food; Shilai also endured death without betraying anyone.

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，累官吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Early in the Wanli reign he rose by stages to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wanli reign he rose to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈吏部尚書，謚文僖。

translations.literal: On death he was posthumously made Minister of Personnel and given the posthumous title Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Minister of Personnel and granted the posthumous title Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 大臨少應舉杭州，鄰婦夜奔，拒之，旦遂徙舍。

translations.literal: In youth when taking the examination at Hangzhou, a neighbor's wife came to him by night; he refused her, and at dawn moved lodgings.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man taking the examination at Hangzhou, a neighbor's wife came to him at night; he refused her and moved lodgings at dawn.

sentences.zh: 為人寬然長者，而內持貞介，不以勢利易。

translations.literal: He was by nature an easygoing elder, yet inwardly held to integrity and did not change for power or profit.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature an easygoing elder, yet inwardly held to integrity and would not bend to power or profit.

sentences.zh: 大順子允淳，與父同登進士。

translations.literal: Dashun's son Yunchun passed the jinshi examination together with his father.
translations.idiomatic: Dashun's son Yunchun passed the jinshi examination in the same year as his father.

sentences.zh: 終尚寶丞。

translations.literal: He ended as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 潘塤，字伯和，山陽人。

translations.literal: Pan Xun, courtesy name Bohe, was a native of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Xun, styled Bohe, was from Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 正德三年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the third year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 授工科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretary of the Ministry of Works section.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works section.

sentences.zh: 性剛決，彈劾無所避。

translations.literal: By nature he was firm and resolute and in impeachment feared nothing.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was firm and resolute and impeached without fear.

sentences.zh: 論諸大寮王鼎、劉機、寧杲、陳天祥等，多見納。

translations.literal: In criticizing great officials such as Wang Ding, Liu Ji, Ning Gao, and Chen Tianxiang, many of his proposals were accepted.
translations.idiomatic: In criticizing great officials such as Wang Ding, Liu Ji, Ning Gao, and Chen Tianxiang, many of his proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 乾清宮災，塤上疏曰：「陛下蒞阼九年，治效未臻，災祥叠見。

translations.literal: When the Qianqing Palace burned, Xun submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty has reigned nine years, yet governance has not reached perfection and omens and disasters appear in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qianqing Palace burned, Xun submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty has reigned nine years, yet good governance has not been achieved and omens and disasters appear in succession.

sentences.zh: 臣願非安宅不居，非大道不由，非正人不親，非儒術不崇，非大閱不觀兵，非執法不成獄，非骨肉之親不幹政，非汗馬之勞不濫賞。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes that Your Majesty will not dwell except in a secure residence, will not follow except the Great Way, will not be intimate except with upright men, will not honor except Confucian learning, will not review troops except at a great inspection, will not complete a case except by enforcing the law, will not allow interference in government except by kin of flesh and blood, and will not grant rewards except for sweat-and-horse merit.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to dwell only in a secure residence, follow only the Great Way, be intimate only with upright men, honor only Confucian learning, review troops only at a great inspection, complete cases only by enforcing the law, allow no interference in government except by close kin, and grant rewards only for genuine military merit.

sentences.zh: 臣聞陛下好戲謔矣。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that Your Majesty loves jesting.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Your Majesty loves jesting.

sentences.zh: 臣以為入而內庭琴瑟鐘鼓人倫之樂，不必遊離宮以為歡，狎群小以為快也；

translations.literal: Your servant considers that within the inner court there are zithers, lutes, bells, and drums—the music of human relations; there is no need to seek delight in wandering palaces or find pleasure in consorting with petty men;
translations.idiomatic: Within the inner court there are zithers, lutes, bells, and drums—the music of human relations; there is no need to seek delight in wandering palaces or find pleasure in consorting with petty men;

sentences.zh: 出而外廷華裔一統莫非臣妾，不必收朝官為私人，集遠人為勇士也。

translations.literal: without, in the outer court all within the civilized realm are Your subjects; there is no need to gather court officials as private retainers or collect distant men as warriors.
translations.idiomatic: outside, all within the civilized realm are Your subjects; there is no need to gather court officials as private retainers or collect distant men as warriors.

sentences.zh: 聞陛下好佛矣。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that Your Majesty loves Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Your Majesty loves Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 臣以為南郊有天地，太廟有祖宗。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that at the southern suburb are Heaven and Earth, and in the Grand Temple are the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: At the southern suburb are Heaven and Earth, and in the Grand Temple are the ancestors.

sentences.zh: 錫祉迎庥，佛於何有？

translations.literal: Blessings granted and favor received—what has Buddhism to do with this?
translations.idiomatic: Blessings granted and favor received—what has Buddhism to do with this?

sentences.zh: 番僧可逐而度僧可止也。

translations.literal: Tibetan monks can be expelled and ordination of monks can be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetan monks can be expelled and ordination of monks can be halted.

sentences.zh: 聞陛下好勇、好貨、好土木矣。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that Your Majesty loves bravery, loves wealth, and loves construction.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Your Majesty loves bravery, loves wealth, and loves construction.

sentences.zh: 臣以為誅奸遏亂，大勇也，不須馳馬試劍以自勞。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that punishing traitors and suppressing disorder is great bravery; there is no need to gallop horses and test swords to weary oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Punishing traitors and suppressing disorder is true bravery; there is no need to gallop horses and test swords to weary oneself.

sentences.zh: 三軍六師，大武也，不須邊將邊軍以自擁。

translations.literal: The Three Armies and Six Divisions are great martial power; there is no need to rely on frontier generals and frontier troops for personal support.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Armies and Six Divisions are the empire's martial power; there is no need to rely on frontier generals and frontier troops for personal support.

sentences.zh: 任土作貢，皇店奚為？

translations.literal: Tribute according to local products—what need is there for imperial shops?
translations.idiomatic: Tribute according to local products—what need is there for imperial shops?

sentences.zh: 阛阓駢闐，內市安用？

translations.literal: Markets crowded and bustling—what use is an inner market?
translations.idiomatic: Markets crowded and bustling—what use is an inner market?

sentences.zh: 阿房壯麗，古以為金塊珠礫也，況養豹乎！

translations.literal: The Epang Palace was magnificent and splendid; the ancients regarded it as gold blocks and pearl rubble—how much more so for keeping leopards!
translations.idiomatic: The Epang Palace was magnificent and splendid; the ancients regarded it as gold blocks and pearl rubble—how much more so for keeping leopards!

sentences.zh: 金碧熒煌，古以為塗膏畔血也，況供佛乎！

translations.literal: Gold and jade glittering— the ancients regarded it as grease spread and blood smeared on fields—how much more so for supplying Buddhism!
translations.idiomatic: Gold and jade glittering—the ancients regarded it as grease spread and blood smeared on fields—how much more so for supplying Buddhism!

sentences.zh: 是數者之好皆可已而不已者也。

translations.literal: These several loves can all be stopped yet are not stopped.
translations.idiomatic: All these indulgences could be stopped, yet they are not.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，報聞。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, acknowledgment was returned.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was submitted, acknowledgment was returned.

sentences.zh: 十一年正月，上書言：「陛下始者血氣未定，禮度或逾。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year he submitted a memorial saying: "At first Your Majesty's vital force was not yet settled and ritual bounds were sometimes exceeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eleventh year he submitted a memorial: "At first Your Majesty's vital force was not yet settled and ritual bounds were sometimes exceeded.

sentences.zh: 今春秋已盛，更弦易轍，此其時也。

translations.literal: Now spring and autumn are already full; it is time to change strings and alter course.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty has reached maturity; it is time to change course.

sentences.zh: 昔太甲居桐，處仁遷義，不失中興。

translations.literal: Formerly Tai Jia dwelt at Tong, dwelling in benevolence and moving in righteousness, and did not lose the restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Tai Jia dwelt at Tong, dwelling in benevolence and moving in righteousness, and did not lose the restoration.

sentences.zh: 漢武下輪臺之詔，年已七十，猶為令主。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han issued the Luntai edict; though already seventy years old, he still became a good ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han issued the Luntai edict; though already seventy years old, he still became a good ruler.

sentences.zh: 況陛下過未浮於太甲，悔又早於武帝，何愆不可蓋，何治不可建乎？

translations.literal: How much more so when Your Majesty's faults do not exceed those of Tai Jia and Your repentance comes earlier than Emperor Wu's—what fault cannot be covered, what governance cannot be established?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's faults do not exceed those of Tai Jia, and Your repentance comes earlier than Emperor Wu's—what fault cannot be remedied, what governance cannot be established?

sentences.zh: 」時欲毀西安門外民居，有所興作。

translations.literal: " At the time the emperor wished to destroy commoners' houses outside Xi'an Gate for construction.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time the emperor wished to destroy commoners' houses outside Xi'an Gate for construction.

sentences.zh: 塤與御史熊相、曹雷復切諫，皆不報。

translations.literal: Xun, together with Censors Xiong Xiang and Cao Lei, again remonstrated forcefully—all went unanswered.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, together with Censors Xiong Xiang and Cao Lei, again remonstrated forcefully, but all went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 三遷至兵科都給事中。

translations.literal: On a third transfer he became chief supervising secretary of the Ministry of War section.
translations.idiomatic: On his third transfer he became chief supervising secretary of the Ministry of War section.

sentences.zh: 右都督毛倫以附劉瑾論死，削世蔭。

translations.literal: Right Chief Commander Mao Lun was sentenced to death for associating with Liu Jin, and hereditary privilege was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Right Chief Commander Mao Lun was sentenced to death for associating with Liu Jin, and hereditary privilege was stripped.

sentences.zh: 倫嘗有德於錢寧，恃為內援，其子求復襲。

translations.literal: Lun had once shown favor to Qian Ning and relied on him as an inner supporter; his son sought restoration of the hereditary rank.
translations.idiomatic: Lun had once shown favor to Qian Ning and relied on him as a palace patron; his son sought restoration of the hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 塤等力爭，寧從中主之，寢其奏。

translations.literal: Xun and others forcefully disputed it; Ning supported it from within, and the memorial was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Xun and others forcefully disputed it; Ning backed it from within, and the memorial was shelved.

sentences.zh: 忽中旨命塤與吏科給事中呂經各進一階，外調，舉朝大駭。

translations.literal: Suddenly an imperial directive ordered Xun and Lu Jing, supervising secretary of the Ministry of Personnel section, each advanced one rank and transferred outside; the whole court was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly an imperial directive ordered Xun and Lu Jing, supervising secretary of the Ministry of Personnel section, each promoted one rank and transferred outside; the whole court was greatly alarmed.

sentences.zh: 給事中邵錫、御史王金等交章請留，不報。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries Shao Xi, Censor Wang Jin, and others submitted memorials in succession requesting that they be kept; no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries Shao Xi, Censor Wang Jin, and others submitted memorials in succession requesting that they be retained, but no reply was given.

sentences.zh: 遂添註塤開州同知。

translations.literal: Xun was then additionally assigned as vice prefect of Kaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was then additionally assigned as vice prefect of Kaizhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉請七年，累官右副都御史，巡撫河南。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiajing he rose by stages to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Jiajing he rose to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and regional governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 潞州巨盜陳卿據青陽山為亂，山西巡撫江潮、常道先後討賊無功，乃敕塤會剿。

translations.literal: The great bandit Chen Qing of Luzhou held Qingyang Mountain in rebellion; Jiang Chao, governor of Shanxi, and Chang Dao successively attacked the bandits without success, so an edict ordered Xun to join in the suppression.
translations.idiomatic: The great bandit Chen Qing of Luzhou held Qingyang Mountain in rebellion; Jiang Chao, governor of Shanxi, and Chang Dao successively attacked the bandits without success, so an edict ordered Xun to join the suppression.

sentences.zh: 塤謀於道曰：「賊守險，難以陣。

translations.literal: Xun plotted with Dao, saying: "The bandits hold the heights and are hard to meet in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Xun plotted with Dao, saying: "The bandits hold the heights and are hard to meet in battle.

sentences.zh: 合諸路夾攻，出不意奪其險，乃可擒也。

translations.literal: Combined forces from all routes attacking from both sides, unexpectedly seizing their stronghold—only then can they be captured.
translations.idiomatic: Forces from all routes must attack from both sides and unexpectedly seize their stronghold—only then can they be captured.

sentences.zh: 」遂分五哨三路入，募土人為導。

translations.literal: " They then divided into five squads and three routes, recruiting locals as guides.
translations.idiomatic: " They then divided into five squads along three routes and recruited locals as guides.

sentences.zh: 首攻奪井腦，賊悉眾爭險。

translations.literal: First they attacked and seized Jingnao; the bandits mustered all their forces to contest the heights.
translations.idiomatic: First they attacked and seized Jingnao; the bandits mustered all their forces to contest the heights.

sentences.zh: 官軍奮擊，大破之，追奔至莎草嶺，毀安陽諸巢。

translations.literal: Government troops fought fiercely and broke them completely, pursuing in flight to Shacao Ridge and destroying the lairs at Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops fought fiercely and routed them, pursuing them to Shacao Ridge and destroying the lairs at Anyang.

sentences.zh: 山東副使牛鸞由潞城入，破賊李莊泉。

translations.literal: Shandong Vice Commissioner Niu Luan entered through Lucheng and broke the bandits at Lizhuang Spring.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong Vice Commissioner Niu Luan entered through Lucheng and defeated the bandits at Lizhuang Spring.

sentences.zh: 其夕，河南副使翟瓚搗卿巢，卿敗走。

translations.literal: That evening Henan Vice Commissioner Zhai Zan raided Qing's lair and Qing fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: That evening Henan Vice Commissioner Zhai Zan raided Qing's lair and Qing fled in defeat.

sentences.zh: 瓚追敗之欒莊山，又敗之神河。

translations.literal: Zan pursued and defeated him at Luanzhuang Mountain and again defeated him at Shenhe.
translations.idiomatic: Zan pursued and defeated him at Luanzhuang Mountain and again at Shenhe.

sentences.zh: 山西僉事陳大綱亦屢蹙賊，先後降二千三百余人。

translations.literal: Shanxi Vice Commissioner Chen Dagang also repeatedly pressed the bandits; in all two thousand three hundred and more surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi Vice Commissioner Chen Dagang also repeatedly pressed the bandits; in all more than 2,300 surrendered.

sentences.zh: 自進兵至搜滅賊巢，凡二十九日。

translations.literal: From advancing troops to searching out and destroying the bandit lairs, it took twenty-nine days in all.
translations.idiomatic: From the advance of troops to the destruction of the bandit lairs, the campaign took twenty-nine days in all.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，帝將大賚，遣給事中夏言往核，未報。

translations.literal: When victory was reported the emperor was about to grant great rewards and sent Supervising Secretary Xia Yan to verify; no reply had yet come.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported the emperor was about to grant great rewards and sent Supervising Secretary Xia Yan to verify the merit; no reply had yet come.

sentences.zh: 河南大饑，塤不以時振，而河南知府範璁不待報，輒開倉發粟，民德而頌之。

translations.literal: Henan suffered great famine; Xun did not provide relief in time, while Henan Prefect Fan Cong, without awaiting authorization, opened the granary and distributed grain—the people were grateful and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Henan suffered a great famine; Xun did not provide relief in time, while Henan Prefect Fan Cong, without awaiting authorization, opened the granary and distributed grain—the people were grateful and praised him.

sentences.zh: 塤怨聲大起，流聞禁中。

translations.literal: Resentment against Xun rose greatly and spread to the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Resentment against Xun rose greatly and reached the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 帝切責撫、按匿災狀。

translations.literal: The emperor sharply rebuked the governor and censor for concealing the disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sharply rebuked the governor and censor for concealing the famine.

sentences.zh: 塤惶恐引罪，且歸罪於璁，遂為給事中蔡經等所劾。

translations.literal: Xun fearfully admitted guilt and also blamed Cong; he was then impeached by Supervising Secretaries Cai Jing and others.
translations.idiomatic: Xun fearfully admitted guilt and also blamed Cong; he was then impeached by Supervising Secretaries Cai Jing and others.

sentences.zh: 詔罷塤，永不敘用。

translations.literal: An edict dismissed Xun and barred him from office forever.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dismissed Xun and permanently barred him from office.

sentences.zh: 言核上平賊功，塤為首。

translations.literal: When Yan verified and reported the merit in suppressing bandits, Xun was ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan verified and reported the merit in suppressing the bandits, Xun was ranked first.

sentences.zh: 桂萼惡之，但賚銀幣。

translations.literal: Gui E hated this and granted only silver and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Gui E disliked this and granted only silver and silks.

sentences.zh: 年八十七卒。

translations.literal: He died at eighty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-seven.

sentences.zh: 呂經，字道夫，陜西寧州人。

translations.literal: Lu Jing, courtesy name Daofu, was a native of Ningzhou in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jing, styled Daofu, was from Ningzhou in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 正德三年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the third year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 授禮科給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretary of the Ministry of Rites section.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Rites section.

sentences.zh: 九年，乾清宮災，經上疏極論義子、番僧、邊帥之害。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when the Qianqing Palace burned, Jing submitted a memorial vigorously discussing the harm of adopted sons, Tibetan monks, and frontier commanders.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when the Qianqing Palace burned, Jing submitted a memorial vigorously discussing the harm of adopted sons, Tibetan monks, and frontier commanders.

sentences.zh: 屢遷吏科都給事中，復極論馬昂女弟入宮事，又劾方面最貪暴者四人。

translations.literal: He rose by stages to chief supervising secretary of the Ministry of Personnel section, again vigorously discussed the matter of Ma Ang's younger sister entering the palace, and also impeached the four most greedy and violent regional officials.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to chief supervising secretary of the Ministry of Personnel section, again vigorously discussed the matter of Ma Ang's younger sister entering the palace, and also impeached the four most greedy and violent regional officials.

sentences.zh: 群小鹹惡，遂謫蒲州同知。

translations.literal: Petty men all hated him, and he was demoted to vice prefect of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men all hated him, and he was demoted to vice prefect of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 又以事忤中官黃玉，誣劾系獄。

translations.literal: Again for a matter he offended the eunuch Huang Yu, who falsely impeached him and had him imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Again, over a matter he offended the eunuch Huang Yu, who falsely impeached him and had him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，擢山東參政。

translations.literal: When the Shizong Emperor ascended the throne he was promoted to vice commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shizong Emperor ascended the throne he was promoted to vice commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十三年累官右副都御史，巡撫遼東。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiajing he rose by stages to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and governor of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Jiajing he rose to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and regional governor of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 故事，每軍一，佐以余丁三；

translations.literal: By precedent, for each army unit one, three auxiliary conscripts were assigned;
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, each army unit was supported by three auxiliary conscripts;

sentences.zh: 每馬一，給牧地五十畝。

translations.literal: for each horse one, fifty mu of pasture land was granted.
translations.idiomatic: for each horse, fifty mu of pasture land was granted.

sentences.zh: 經損余丁之二編入均徭冊，盡收牧地還官。

translations.literal: Jing reduced two-thirds of the auxiliary conscripts and entered them in the equal-corvée register, and reclaimed all pasture land for the government.
translations.idiomatic: Jing cut auxiliary conscripts by two-thirds and entered them in the equal-corvée register, and reclaimed all pasture land for the government.

sentences.zh: 又役軍築邊墻，督趣過當。

translations.literal: He also conscripted troops to build the frontier wall, pressing them excessively.
translations.idiomatic: He also conscripted troops to build the frontier wall and drove them excessively hard.

sentences.zh: 諸軍詣經乞罷役，都指揮劉尚德叱之不退，經呼左右榜訴者。

translations.literal: The troops went to Jing begging to be released from labor; Chief Commander Liu Shangde shouted at them but they would not withdraw, and Jing called attendants to beat the complainants.
translations.idiomatic: The troops petitioned Jing to be released from labor; Chief Commander Liu Shangde shouted at them but they would not withdraw, and Jing called attendants to beat the complainants.

sentences.zh: 卒遂爭毆尚德，經竄苑馬寺幽室中。

translations.literal: The soldiers then fought and beat Shangde; Jing fled into a secluded room at the Stud Farm Office.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers then fought and beat Shangde; Jing fled into a secluded room at the Stud Farm Office.

sentences.zh: 亂卒毀府門，火均徭冊，搜得經，裂其冠裳，幽之都司署。

translations.literal: The mutinous soldiers destroyed the government gate, burned the equal-corvée register, found Jing, tore his cap and robes, and confined him at the regional commander's office.
translations.idiomatic: The mutinous soldiers destroyed the government gate, burned the equal-corvée register, found Jing, tore off his cap and robes, and confined him at the regional commander's office.

sentences.zh: 帝詔經還朝。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Jing to return to court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Jing to return to court.

sentences.zh: 都指揮袁璘將克諸軍草價為辦裝，卒復執經，裸而置之獄，虐辱之，脅鎮守中官王純等奏經十一罪。

translations.literal: Chief Commander Yuan Lin was about to collect fodder money from the troops to pay travel expenses; the soldiers again seized Jing, stripped him naked and put him in prison, abused and humiliated him, and coerced the garrison eunuch Wang Chun and others to memorialize eleven charges against Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Commander Yuan Lin was about to collect fodder money from the troops for travel expenses; the soldiers again seized Jing, stripped him naked and imprisoned him, abused and humiliated him, and coerced the garrison eunuch Wang Chun and others to memorialize eleven charges against Jing.

sentences.zh: 帝逮經。

translations.literal: The emperor had Jing arrested.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Jing arrested.

sentences.zh: 亂卒復置官校於獄，久之始解。

translations.literal: The mutinous soldiers again placed official attendants in prison; only after a long time were they released.
translations.idiomatic: The mutinous soldiers again imprisoned official attendants; only after a long time were they released.

sentences.zh: 經下詔獄，謫戍茂州。

translations.literal: Jing was put in the imperial prison and banished to garrison at Maozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was imprisoned and exiled to Maozhou as a soldier.

sentences.zh: 數年釋還。

translations.literal: After several years he was released and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he was released and returned home.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，復官，卒。

translations.literal: Early in Longqing he was restored to office and died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Longqing reign he was restored to office and died.

sentences.zh: 亂卒為曾銑所定，見《銑傳》。

translations.literal: The mutinous soldiers were suppressed by Zeng Xuan; see the biography of Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: The mutinous soldiers were suppressed by Zeng Xuan; see the biography of Xuan.

sentences.zh: 歐陽重，字子重，廬陵人。

translations.literal: Ouyang Zhong, courtesy name Zizhong, was a native of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Zhong, styled Zizhong, was from Luling.

sentences.zh: 正德三年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the third year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 殿試對策，歷詆闕政。

translations.literal: In the palace examination policy essay he successively denounced failures of government.
translations.idiomatic: In the palace examination policy essay he successively denounced failures of government.

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾兄死，百官往吊，重不往。

translations.literal: When Liu Jin's elder brother died, all officials went to offer condolences; Zhong did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jin's elder brother died, all officials went to offer condolences; Zhong did not go.

sentences.zh: 張銳、錢寧掌廠衛，連構搢紳獄，重皆力與爭。

translations.literal: Zhang Rui and Qian Ning controlled the Brocade Guard and repeatedly framed officials in prison; Zhong forcefully disputed each case.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rui and Qian Ning controlled the Brocade Guard and repeatedly framed officials in prison; Zhong forcefully disputed each case.

sentences.zh: 銳等假他事系之獄，贖杖還職，仍停俸。

translations.literal: Rui and others imprisoned him on other charges; he redeemed himself by beating and returned to office, but salary was still suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Rui and others imprisoned him on other charges; he redeemed himself by beating and returned to office, but his salary was still suspended.

sentences.zh: 再遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to department director.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to department director.

sentences.zh: 歷四川、雲南提學副使。

translations.literal: He served as vice education commissioner of Sichuan and Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice education commissioner of Sichuan and Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 遷浙江按察使，未上。

translations.literal: He was transferred to surveillance commissioner of Zhejiang but had not yet reported.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to surveillance commissioner of Zhejiang but had not yet reported.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖六年春拜右僉都御史，巡撫應天。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year of Jiajing he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and governor of Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year of Jiajing he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and regional governor of Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 會尋甸土酋安銓、鳳朝文反，廷議以重諳滇事，乃改雲南。

translations.literal: As the native chieftain An Quan of Xundian and Feng Chaowen rebelled, the court considered that Zhong was familiar with Yunnan affairs and changed his assignment to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: As the native chieftain An Quan of Xundian and Feng Chaowen rebelled, the court considered Zhong familiar with Yunnan affairs and reassigned him to Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 初，武定土知府鳳詔母子坐事留雲南，朝文紿其眾，言詔已戮，官軍將盡滅其部黨，以故諸蠻悉從為亂，攻圍會城。

translations.literal: Earlier the native prefect Feng Zhao and his mother of Wuding, having been implicated in a case, were detained in Yunnan; Chaowen deceived the masses, saying Zhao had already been executed and that government troops would exterminate all his followers, so all the tribes joined the rebellion and besieged the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the native prefect Feng Zhao and his mother of Wuding, implicated in a case, were detained in Yunnan; Chaowen deceived the masses, claiming Zhao had been executed and that government troops would exterminate all his followers, so the tribes joined the rebellion and besieged the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 重督兵擊敗之，而遣詔母子還故地。

translations.literal: Zhong supervised troops, defeated them, and sent Zhao and his mother back to their former territory.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong supervised troops, defeated the rebels, and sent Zhao and his mother back to their former territory.

sentences.zh: 其黨愕，相率歸之。

translations.literal: Their followers were astonished and returned to them in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Their followers were astonished and returned to them in succession.

sentences.zh: 朝文計窮，絕普渡河走。

translations.literal: Chaowen's plans exhausted, he crossed the Pudu River and fled.
translations.idiomatic: With his plans exhausted, Chaowen crossed the Pudu River and fled.

sentences.zh: 追兵至，殲焉。

translations.literal: Pursuing troops arrived and annihilated him.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing troops arrived and annihilated him.

sentences.zh: 銓逃尋甸故巢。

translations.literal: Quan fled to his old lair in Xundian.
translations.idiomatic: Quan fled to his old lair in Xundian.

sentences.zh: 官軍攻破其砦，執銓，賊盡平。

translations.literal: Government troops broke their stockade and captured Quan; the bandits were completely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops broke their stockade and captured Quan; the rebels were completely pacified.

sentences.zh: 乃散其黨二萬人，遷尋甸府於鳳梧山下，更設守禦千戶所。

translations.literal: He then dispersed their twenty thousand followers, moved the Xundian prefecture to below Fengwu Mountain, and established a new defense garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He then dispersed their twenty thousand followers, moved the Xundian prefecture to below Fengwu Mountain, and established a new defense garrison.

sentences.zh: 重推功於前撫臣傅習，並進秩任子。

translations.literal: Zhong attributed merit to the former governor Fu Xi and recommended rank advancement and appointment of a son to office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong attributed merit to the former governor Fu Xi and recommended rank advancement and appointment of a son to office.

sentences.zh: 緬甸、木邦、隴川、孟密、孟養諸酋相仇殺，各訐奏於朝，下重等勘覆。

translations.literal: The chieftains of Burma, Mubang, Longchuan, Mengmi, and Mengyang mutually killed one another and each denounced the other at court; the court ordered Zhong and others to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftains of Burma, Mubang, Longchuan, Mengmi, and Mengyang mutually killed one another and each denounced the other at court; the court ordered Zhong and others to investigate.

sentences.zh: 遣參政王汝舟、知府嚴時泰等遍歷諸蠻，譬以禍福。

translations.literal: He sent Vice Commissioner Wang Ruzhou, Prefect Yan Shitai, and others to travel through all the tribes, admonishing them with warnings of disaster and blessing.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Vice Commissioner Wang Ruzhou, Prefect Yan Shitai, and others to travel through all the tribes, admonishing them with warnings of disaster and blessing.

sentences.zh: 皆還侵地，供貢如故。

translations.literal: All returned invaded territory and offered tribute as before.
translations.idiomatic: All returned invaded territory and offered tribute as before.

sentences.zh: 重列善後數事，悉報可，賜璽書褒諭。

translations.literal: Zhong listed several follow-up measures; all were approved and an imperial letter of commendation was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong listed several follow-up measures; all were approved and an imperial letter of commendation was granted.

sentences.zh: 重乃恤創殘，振貧乏，輕徭賦，規畫鹽鐵商稅、屯田諸務。

translations.literal: Zhong then comforted the wounded, relieved the impoverished, lightened corvée and tax, and planned salt, iron, commercial tax, and garrison-field affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong then comforted the wounded, relieved the impoverished, lightened corvée and tax, and planned salt, iron, commercial tax, and garrison-field affairs.

sentences.zh: 民鹹便之。

translations.literal: The people all found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The people all found it convenient.

sentences.zh: 雲南歲貢金千兩，費不貲。

translations.literal: Yunnan annually tribute gold of one thousand taels, at immeasurable cost.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan annually tribute gold of one thousand taels, at immeasurable cost.

sentences.zh: 大理太和蒼山產奇石，鎮守中官遣軍匠攻鑿。

translations.literal: Cangshan in Dali Taihe produced strange stones; the garrison eunuch sent soldiers and craftsmen to quarry them.
translations.idiomatic: Cangshan in Dali Taihe produced strange stones; the garrison eunuch sent soldiers and craftsmen to quarry them.

sentences.zh: 山崩，壓死無算。

translations.literal: The mountain collapsed and countless were crushed to death.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain collapsed and countless people were crushed to death.

sentences.zh: 重皆疏罷之，浮費大省。

translations.literal: Zhong memorialized to stop all these; superfluous expenses were greatly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong memorialized to stop all these; superfluous expenses were greatly reduced.

sentences.zh: 當是時，鎮守太監杜唐、黔國公沐紹勛相比為奸利，長吏不敢問，群盜由此起。

translations.literal: At the time Garrison Eunuch Du Tang and Duke of Qian State Mu Shaoxun mutually aided one another in illicit profit; senior officials dared not inquire, and bandits arose from this.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Garrison Eunuch Du Tang and Duke of Qian State Mu Shaoxun mutually aided one another in illicit profit; senior officials dared not inquire, and bandits arose from this.

sentences.zh: 重疏言：盜率唐、紹勛莊戶，請究主者。

translations.literal: Zhong memorialized: bandits mostly came from Tang's and Shaoxun's estate households; he requested investigation of the masters.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong memorialized: the bandits mostly came from Tang's and Shaoxun's estate households; he requested investigation of those responsible.

sentences.zh: 又奏紹勛任千戶何經廣誘奸人，奪民產；

translations.literal: He also memorialized that Shaoxun had his company commander He Jingguang entice wicked men and seize commoners' property;
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized that Shaoxun had his company commander He Jingguang entice wicked men and seize commoners' property;

sentences.zh: 唐役占官軍，歲取財萬計。

translations.literal: Tang conscripted and occupied government troops, annually taking wealth in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Tang conscripted and occupied government troops, annually taking wealth in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 因極言鎮守中官宜革。

translations.literal: He therefore vigorously argued that garrison eunuchs ought to be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore vigorously argued that garrison eunuchs ought to be abolished.

sentences.zh: 帝頗納其言，頻下詔飭紹勛，命唐還京待勘。

translations.literal: The emperor largely accepted his words, repeatedly issued edicts to admonish Shaoxun, and ordered Tang to return to the capital pending investigation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor largely accepted his words, repeatedly issued edicts to admonish Shaoxun, and ordered Tang to return to the capital pending investigation.

sentences.zh: 二人懼且怒，遣人結張璁，謀去重。

translations.literal: The two feared and grew angry, sent men to connect with Zhang Cong, and plotted to remove Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: The two feared and grew angry, sent men to connect with Zhang Cong, and plotted to remove Zhong.

sentences.zh: 會重奉命清異姓冒軍弊，都司久未報，給餉後期。

translations.literal: As Zhong was ordered to clear the abuse of non-kin falsely enrolled in the army, the regional command had long not reported, and rations were paid late.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhong was ordered to clear the abuse of non-kin falsely enrolled in the army, the regional command had long not reported, and rations were paid late.

sentences.zh: 唐等遂嗾六衛軍嘩於軍門。

translations.literal: Tang and others then incited the six garrison guards to riot at the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: Tang and others then incited the six garrison guards to riot at the army gate.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史劉臬以聞。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Liu Nie reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Liu Nie reported it.

sentences.zh: 劾重及唐、紹勛處置失當。

translations.literal: He impeached Zhong and Tang and Shaoxun for improper handling.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Zhong, Tang, and Shaoxun for improper handling.

sentences.zh: 璁從中主之，解重職，責臬黨庇，調外任，唐、紹勛不問。

translations.literal: Cong supported it from within; Zhong was removed from office, Nie was blamed for factional protection and transferred to an outside post, and Tang and Shaoxun were not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Cong supported it from within; Zhong was removed from office, Nie was blamed for factional protection and transferred to an outside post, and Tang and Shaoxun were not questioned.

sentences.zh: 都給事中夏言等抗章曰：「以軍士噪罪撫、按，紀綱謂何？

translations.literal: Chief Supervising Secretary Xia Yan and others submitted a forceful memorial saying: "To punish governor and censor because soldiers made a disturbance—what does this mean for discipline?
translations.idiomatic: Chief Supervising Secretary Xia Yan and others submitted a forceful memorial: "To punish the governor and censor because soldiers made a disturbance—what does this mean for discipline?

sentences.zh: 況重奉詔非生事。

translations.literal: Moreover Zhong acted on imperial order and did not create trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Zhong acted on imperial order and did not create trouble.

sentences.zh: 臬言唐、紹勛罪與重等，今處分失宜，無以服天下。

translations.literal: Nie said Tang's and Shaoxun's crimes were equal to Zhong's; now the disposition is improper and cannot satisfy the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Nie said Tang's and Shaoxun's crimes were equal to Zhong's; now the disposition is improper and cannot satisfy the realm.

sentences.zh: 頃年士卒驕悍，相效成風，類以月糧借口。

translations.literal: In recent years soldiers have grown arrogant and fierce, imitating one another until it became custom, generally using monthly rations as a pretext.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years soldiers have grown arrogant and fierce, imitating one another until it became custom, generally using monthly rations as a pretext.

sentences.zh: 如甘肅、大同、福州、保定，事變屢見。

translations.literal: At Gansu, Datong, Fuzhou, and Baoding, disturbances repeatedly appeared.
translations.idiomatic: At Gansu, Datong, Fuzhou, and Baoding, disturbances repeatedly appeared.

sentences.zh: 失今不治，他日當事之臣以此為諱，專務姑息，孰肯為陛下任事哉！

translations.literal: If not corrected now, future officials will take this as a taboo, specialize in indulgence, and who will be willing to serve Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: If not corrected now, future officials will take this as a taboo, specialize in indulgence, and who will be willing to serve Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 願曲宥二臣，全朝廷之體。

translations.literal: We wish that the two officials be graciously pardoned to preserve the dignity of the court.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the two officials be graciously pardoned to preserve the dignity of the court.

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，奪言等俸。

translations.literal: " The emperor was enraged and stripped Yan and others of salary.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was enraged and stripped Yan and others of salary.

sentences.zh: 重罷歸在道，聞御史王化劾其為桂萼黨，不勝忿，抗疏陳辨，請錄「大禮」大獄被逐諸臣，而自乞褫職。

translations.literal: Zhong, dismissed and returning home on the road, heard that Censor Wang Hua impeached him as a partisan of Gui E; unable to bear the anger, he submitted a forceful memorial in self-defense, requesting that officials expelled in the Great Rites major cases be recorded, and himself begged to be stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong, dismissed and returning home on the road, heard that Censor Wang Hua impeached him as a partisan of Gui E; unable to bear the anger, he submitted a forceful memorial in self-defense, requesting that officials expelled in the "Great Rites" major cases be recorded, and himself begged to be stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 又言得紹勛所遣百戶丁鎮私書，知行賄張璁，乞其覆護；

translations.literal: He also said he obtained a private letter sent by Shaoxun's company commander Ding Zhen, knowing he bribed Zhang Cong and begged his protection;
translations.idiomatic: He also said he obtained a private letter sent by Shaoxun's company commander Ding Zhen, showing he bribed Zhang Cong and begged his protection;

sentences.zh: 璁奸佞，不宜在左右。

translations.literal: Cong was treacherous and flattering and ought not remain at the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was treacherous and flattering and ought not remain at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 璁疏辨。

translations.literal: Cong submitted a memorial in self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Cong submitted a memorial in self-defense.

sentences.zh: 帝以重失職怨望，黜為民。

translations.literal: The emperor considered that Zhong, having lost office, harbored resentment and demoted him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor considered that Zhong, having lost office, harbored resentment and demoted him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 重以臬被謫，言等奪俸，皆由己致之，復疏乞重譴代言官罪。

translations.literal: Zhong, because Nie was demoted and Yan and others lost salary—all caused by himself—again memorialized begging heavy punishment for himself in place of the remonstrance officials.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong, because Nie was demoted and Yan and others lost salary—all caused by himself—again memorialized begging heavy punishment for himself in place of the remonstrance officials.

sentences.zh: 帝益怒，以已除名，置不問。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angrier; as Zhong was already struck from the rolls, he set it aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angrier; as Zhong was already struck from the rolls, he set it aside without inquiry.

sentences.zh: 重家居二十余年，言者屢薦，竟不復召。

translations.literal: Zhong lived at home more than twenty years; remonstrators repeatedly recommended him, yet he was never recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong lived at home for more than twenty years; remonstrators repeatedly recommended him, yet he was never recalled.

sentences.zh: 朱裳，字公垂，沙河人。

translations.literal: Zhu Shang, courtesy name Gongchui, was a native of Shahe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shang, styled Gongchui, was from Shahe.

sentences.zh: 年十四為諸生，讀書黌舍，躬執爨。

translations.literal: At fourteen he became a student and, reading in the school hall, personally tended the cooking fire.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he became a student and, reading in the school hall, personally tended the cooking fire.
